questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking country, far away.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We got many e-mails, so found it relatively easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Opening meetings with exchange student coordinators.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I used
flatmates.com
to find places. Tried finding something in advance, did not work out, so I arrived two weeks before anything uni-related began to look for flatshares. Then I got heaps of responses, so arrive early to go hunting for a home! Pay for a subscribtion to flatmates, it is worth it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Usually way cheaper than using student accomodation! Prioritise living close-ish to campus and with people renting out a room rather than some agency. 

Also, houses get extremely cold in the winter (badly built), so pack a warm pyjamas and warm socks!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My flatmates ended up becoming my best friends here, so definitely spend time looking for a spot that suits you. Also great way to get friends that are local lol

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far as I remember you get an e-mail where you have to pick your courses. The first week of classes you can still change units, so don't stress it too much.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International students coordinator hosted a in person and zoom meeting for questions I think.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Play around with your schedule and move tutorials! I was able to create a schedule without to many holes and days that were fully off because I spent quite a lot of time moving stuff around.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mostly took first year courses as I wanted to do something different from my degree. Would recommend, definitely also helped with the workload not being as intense later in the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Shorter lectures accompanied by tutorials. 
Was definitely challenged by the workload, as I am used to one big final exam at the end, but at USYD the workload is spread across the semester in smaller assignments and presentations. Just something to get used to, and quite nice that your final assignment at the end of the semester won't determine your whole grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ARHT1001: Style and Substance: Introducing Art History 
FILM2002: Film Genre, Genre Film
GCST1601: Culture, Power, Identity 
INDG1001: Introduction to Indigenous Cultures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
"INDG1001: Introduction to Indigenous Cultures" is very uniquely Australian and teaches you a lot about important Aboriginal history and culture. Very vital in my understanding of Australian society. 
Art history was also very fun and educational, great lecturers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hostel stay for the first few weeks before finding accomodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Get a concession card for Opal (public transport)!!! Will cut down public transport costs in half.

Food and groceries are generally slightly cheaper. Also almost all museums are free, take advantage of that.

Housing is generally pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs. A few events the first couple of weeks, good way to meet especially other international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Film society! Very much recommended, on every week and everyone is chatty. Made many friends there. 
Also go on the free USU day trips, good way to meet people and cool trips (for free).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on many foreshore walks! Close to Sydney is Blue Mountains, very cool nature. Take the train to Kiama + Wollongong to see something out of Sydney.

For longer breaks, go to Tasmania! Very different vibe and cool nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Slang is weird, but aussies are more than happy to explain.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Talk to people in class! Other students are also just trying to make friends, and it's really nice to have a buddy in class. 

Join societies and clubs! Even if it's not fully your thing, just go for the first few weeks to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Students are generally quite young when starting uni in Australia, so if you're older than 20, you might be the oldest in your class. Nothing to do about it, so just be prepared to hang out with some teenagers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: General friendliness and openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the paid version of flatmates to get more responses. Go on hikes and  appreciate the cool nature and beaches. 
Talk to people! Aussies are generally very friendly and curious on people from other countries, so don't be afraid to just go up to someone and chat. You're on a different continent, so who cares if it's a little embarrassing!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: WEAR SUNSCREEN! No ozone layer in Australia, so get SPF 50, and don't bother bringing anything from home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting new people and getting a routine on the other side of the world. 

Travelling to new places in Australia and seeing incredible nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Going home and leaving your new friends behind :(

Also getting used to a different academic system, but you'll manage!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
